text:
nina: Quick hypothesis: lightweight speculative decode on 4-bit quant models will recover ~60-80% of the latency win vs FP16 while keeping quality regression <2 pts on our MMLU subset. propose a 6-hour quickbake A/B: baseline=FP16 static batch, variant=4-bit+speculative with 1-token lookahead.
sam: sounds reasonable. define metrics we care about (P95 latency, tokens/s cost, MMLU mean accuracy, and a small safety/toxicity smoke).
liam: also add model failure rate (timeouts, OOMs) and token emission divergence (KL or BLEU vs baseline). product wants concrete numbers for potential docs.
nina: plan: run 10k eval prompts (mixed slices: short/medium/long), collect streaming P50/P95, per-example MMLU, and delta-human for 200 sampled completions. can we get infra for the run tonight?
anya: I can reserve a dedicated pool for 8 hours on the 70B-quant runners. schedule window 23:00-07:00 UTC? that avoids peak.
sam: experiment config (quick):
```
MODEL=redwood-70b-4bit-q
DECODE=strategy=speculative,lookahead=1,timeout_ms=800
BATCH=1
EVAL_SET=mmlu-10k-mix
METRICS=latency,p95,tokens_per_usd,mmlu,divergence
```
we should also run a control with `DECODE=strategy=standard` and same quant.
kevin: small caveat: our 4-bit runtime currently falls back to slower kernels for long sequences (>2048) which will bias P95. either clip sequences or tag by length in analysis.
sam: good catch. add a per-length bucket: <512, 512-2048, >2048. report separate P95 per bucket.
deploy-bot: experiment job queued: exp-2756001111-quickbake on pool=70b-4bit-dedicated, est time=6h. logs: https://ci.redwood/test/exp-2756001111
liam: for the human eval subset, can we force greedy vs sampling differences? need to know if spec introduces safety shifts.
nina: yes force same sampling params across arms; speculative only affects runtime ordering, not random seed. will sample 200 seeds across prompts.
anya: started warmup scripts now, warming kv-cache and running microbenchmarks. observed token throughput +2.7x on short sequences in warmup vs baseline (roughly matching hypothesis).
kevin: preliminary synthetic numbers (from microbench): FP16 P95=120ms, 4-bit standard P95=75ms, 4-bit+spec P95=48ms (short seq). note: cost reduction estimate ~55% tokens/USD but need full run to confirm.
sam: remind: quality regression threshold is 2 pts absolute MMLU drop. if >2 we fail the quickbake and need to tune lookahead or fallback policy.
liam: also flag any prompt categories where hallucination increases >5% or toxicity score changes.
nina: running now. I'll post the first 1k prompt quick summary in ~45m.
(45m later)
deploy-bot: exp-2756001111-quickbake: partial results uploaded to artifacts. summary: 1k/10k done. link: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/exp-2756001111/part1.json
sam: skimmed the artifact: short-seq P95 numbers look solid; MMLU delta ~-0.9 pts on short, -1.8 on medium, but on >2048 samples delta jumps to -3.4 (as kevin warned).
kevin: hypothesis: kernel fallback and speculative prefetch misalignment for long kv caches. two mitigations: increase lookahead to 2 for long seqs or force non-spec for >2048.
nina: agree. quick AB within run: switching long>2048 to lookahead=2 for next chunk. will re-run those bucket only.
anya: reconfig applied; next batch scheduled. ETA ~40m.
sam: also add delta perplexity and a quick BLEU-like overlap for completions to quantify divergence.
liam: good. also prepare a short note for eng docs summarizing when to use speculative on quant models and when to prefer standard decode.
kevin: one more operational note: watch for increased KV cache memory churn with lookahead>1 on quant runner; it can spike GPU mem and cause throttling.
nina: noted. I'll cap concurrency for that bucket.
(2h later)
deploy-bot: exp-2756001111-quickbake: full run complete. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/exp-2756001111/full_report.json
sam: quick readout: overall MMLU delta = -1.1 pts; cost reduction ~52%; P95 overall down from 120ms->58ms. >2048 bucket still -2.6 pts with lookahead=2 (improved from -3.4). long-bucket accounts for 8% of requests in our production distribution.
liam: so net impact is acceptable for many customers but we need an explicit rollout rule: avoid speculative on model variants serving >2048 median seq length or allow opt-in.
kevin: create a fallback policy: when seq_len_estimate > 2048 or mem_pressure=true => decode=standard. otherwise enable speculative with lookahead=1.
nina: will draft a short RFC and a script to auto-classify routes based on recent seq length histograms.
anya: I can hook the script to the console so teams can preview expected gains per route.
sam: next steps: run a targeted safety eval on the 200 human samples to check subtle shifts, then push a canary with traffic=1% for two days if results look stable.
liam: thanks everyone. nice pragmatic bakeoff. :tada:
kevin: documented kernel caveats in the ticket.
nina: uploading final notes and the quick configuration snippets to the experiment ticket: https://go/redwood/ticket/EX-2756
(remaining chatter: thumbs up reactions and a few single-line clarifications)
